The interaction of Welchol with oral contraceptives containing norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol is not available. Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, and Impairment of Fertility 8. A 104-week carcinogenicity study in CD-1 mice using colesevelam hydrochloride at oral dietary doses up to 3 g/kg/day (approximately 50 times the maximum recommended human dose of 4.5 g/day based on body weight) showed no significant drug-induced tumor findings in male or female mice. 9. In a 104-week carcinogenicity study in Harlan Sprague-Dawley rats, a statistically significant increase in pancreatic acinar cell adenomas was observed in male rats at doses greater than 1.2 g/kg/day (approximately 20 times the maximum human dose based on body weight). 10. A statistically significant increase in thyroid C-cell adenomas was observed in female rats at 2.4 g/kg/day (approximately 40 times the maximum human dose based on body weight). 11. Colesevelam hydrochloride and its four degradants were evaluated for mutagenicity using the Ames test and a mammalian chromosomal aberration test. 12. The four degradants and an extract of the parent compound did not exhibit genetic toxicity in an in vitro bacterial mutagenesis assay (Ames assay) using S. typhimurium and E. coli, with or without rat liver metabolic activation. 13. An extract of the parent compound was positive in the Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cell chromosomal aberration assay in the presence of metabolic activation but negative in its absence. 14. Two of the four degradants (decylamine HCl and aminohexyltrimethylammonium chloride HCl) showed equivocal results in the CHO cell chromosomal aberration assay without metabolic activation and were negative with metabolic activation. 15. The other two degradants (didecylamine HCl and 6-decylamino-hexyltrimethylammonium chloride HCl) were negative in the CHO cell chromosomal aberration assay both with and without metabolic activation. 16. Colesevelam hydrochloride did not impair fertility in rats at doses up to 3 g/kg/day (approximately 50 times the maximum human dose based on body weight). Animal Toxicology and Pharmacology 17. Reproductive toxicity studies in rats and rabbits at doses up to 3 g/kg/day and 1 g/kg/day, respectively (approximately 50 and 17 times the maximum human dose based on body weight), revealed no evidence of harm to the fetus due to colesevelam hydrochloride. Clinical Studies Primary Hyperlipidemia 18. Welchol reduces total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), apolipoprotein B (Apo B), and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C) when administered alone or in combination with a statin in patients with primary hyperlipidemia. 19. Approximately 1,600 patients were studied in nine clinical trials with treatment durations ranging from 4 to 50 weeks. 20. Except for one open-label, uncontrolled, long-term extension study, all studies were multicenter, randomized, double-blind, and placebo-controlled. 21. The maximum therapeutic response to Welchol was achieved within 2 weeks and maintained during long-term therapy. Monotherapy 22. In a study of patients with LDL-C levels between 130 mg/dL and 220 mg/dL (mean 158 mg/dL), Welchol was administered for 24 weeks in divided doses with morning and evening meals. 23. Mean LDL-C reductions were 15% and 18% at doses of 3.8 g and 4.5 g, respectively. 24. Mean TC reductions were 7% and 10%, respectively. 25. Mean Apo B reductions were 12% in both treatment groups. 26. Welchol increased HDL-C by 3% at both doses. 27. Increases in triglycerides (TG) of 9-10% were observed at both doses, but these changes were not statistically different from placebo. Combination Therapy 28. Co-administration of Welchol with a statin (atorvastatin, lovastatin, or simvastatin) in three clinical studies demonstrated an additive reduction in LDL-C. 29. Welchol doses of 2.3 g to 3.8 g resulted in an additional 8% to 16% reduction in LDL-C beyond that achieved with the statin alone. 30. The LDL-C reduction achieved with the combination of Welchol and any given dose of statin therapy was statistically superior to that achieved with Welchol or the statin alone. Pediatric Therapy 31. The safety and efficacy of Welchol in pediatric patients were evaluated in an 8-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study followed by an open-label phase in 194 boys and postmenarchal girls aged 10-17 years with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (heFH). 32. During the double-blind treatment period, patients were randomly assigned to receive Welchol 3.8 g/day, Welchol 1.9 g/day, or placebo. 33. After 8 weeks of treatment, Welchol 3.8 g/day significantly decreased plasma levels of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, TC, and Apo B and significantly increased HDL-C. 34. A moderate, non-statistically significant increase in TG was observed compared to placebo.
